item.title: Undertone 1.39.10
item.description:
• Briefings no longer mix in notes from unrelated meetings when your own name is in the meeting's title ("You and Paul").

Undertone 1.39.9

  • Interview scores learn from what really happened: mark whether you moved forward, or Undertone sees a later meeting with the same company, and future predictions calibrate against it.
  • Prep's coaching shows how many interview calls were right.

Undertone 1.39.8

  • Deadlines on Home no longer pick up another company's plans, like a roadmap described in a job interview.

Undertone 1.39.7

  • The right meeting when two overlap. When two calendar meetings start at the same time, Undertone now picks a required one over an "[Optional]" one, and checks at the end of the call which one was really discussed (names and topics said), filing it under that one.
  • Your answers are kept when your voice comes back in the call audio. If your own voice also plays through the call (another device in the room, a call app that plays you back), Undertone used to drop your lines as echo. It now tells your voice from speaker echo by timing and loudness, so your questions and answers are captured and can be coached.

Undertone 1.39.6

  • Coaching in Prep. One overall score from how you answered in past meetings and interviews (recent ones count most), how it's moving, your score history, and a coaching plan written from all of it: what to work on, a drill for each, and how to prepare for what's next.
  • Feedback you were given. When someone in a meeting gives you feedback or a rating ("7 out of 10"), Undertone now notes it with the meeting's score and uses it in your plan.
  • Score recent meetings. Meetings that were never scored can be scored from Prep in one click.

Undertone 1.39.1

  • Meetings you organize are now recognised as yours on Google and Exchange calendars too, so "I'm presenting" turns on by itself and the slides get made without a click. You can still switch it off for any meeting.

Undertone 1.39.0

  • Talking points before every meeting, without a click. Half an hour before a meeting, Undertone writes a full talking-points document: what to say in order with time for each part, the evidence with real ticket keys, numbers and dates, the decisions needed and who owns them, the timeline, and a close. Every fact names its source.
  • Memory first, then your sources. Undertone checks its own memory (past meetings, recaps, tasks, glossary, what you told Ask) first, then searches every source you've connected, such as Granola, Jira, Slack, Notion, Linear, Confluence or Drive. It only reads; it never posts or edits anything.
  • Prep notes for you. Each document ends with the objections to expect and suggested answers, plus loose ends to tidy up first, like tickets still in Backlog or unanswered threads.
  • Slides when you present. For meetings you organize, or when you switch on "I'm presenting", a short slide deck made from the talking points is waiting in Artifacts. Present it or export it from there.
  • Kept up to date. If the meeting moves, the invite changes or something new comes up in Undertone, the talking points are rewritten on their own, at most twice per meeting, so credits aren't wasted. Prep questions now come from the talking points.
